content.comment_body: My post was moved from the [product_name] forum to the general [product_name] forum, but it belongs here. I'm working on displaying and editing start/stop times from a weekly timer set in a [product_name] module using the HMI panel. This is my first time with [product_name] and this is the only issue I'm stuck with. Any help is welcome. Thank you.

Hello, First, configure your start and stop times using [product_name] in the VM Mapping section. Next, set up the connection in [product_name] Flexible, choosing the correct communication driver. Then, define your variables and use the same addresses as in [product_name]. I've attached a screenshot, but I use [product_name] V11; however, the process should be similar in [product_name] Flexible. Also, have a look at this [url]: How to set up a connection between [product_name] and an HMI Panel? Hope this helps. Best regards, [user_name]

Thanks, but this is the standard advice given when asking about [product_name] integration with [product_name]. I get the impression even moderators lack hands-on experience with this setup. What I need is to read the memory address where the timer's start/stop times are stored and display this in HH:MM format. The memory is in word format, and I need to extract 4 bits at a time and show them as decimal values. Does anyone know how to do this?

I see what you're trying to achieve, but it's not straightforward. As far as I know, start/stop times can only be stored in a Word. One idea is to use memory VW0, where hours go in vb0 and minutes in vb1, but they're not stored as decimal values. You could create a text list with all possible time values and their corresponding decimal representations. Then display two symbolic I/O fields using this text list and connect them to the hour and minute tags. Hope this helps clarify the approach.

If the field is open for editing, you can change the I/O field's display format to "Hexadecimal" so you can enter times in the "hhmm" format. This prevents invalid entries like letters A to F or values beyond valid hours/minutes.
Hello, I have the same issue. Were you able to resolve it? [user_name]

The process is complex for first-time or less experienced users, requiring advanced configuration and workarounds. Most advice provided is generic or demands significant manual setup, which frustrates users.
